features.title: Single reasoning agent
features.detail: One reasoning agent owns strategy and tool choice while the runtime owns governed execution and lifecycle truth.

features.title: Structured provider/tool loop
features.detail: Typed tool calls, runtime observations and bounded re-entry are part of the current agent architecture.

features.title: Browser conversation instruction ownership
features.detail: The browser conversation is the instruction surface and the relay submits detected assistant turns into the governed agent runtime.

features.title: Non-terminal provider readiness preflight
features.detail: Recovery-only readiness checks retain startup ownership with checking_provider instead of projecting a terminal stopped state.

features.title: Fresh app-session isolation
features.detail: Fresh runtime reset clears only active current-session ownership while preserving historical session evidence; the first fresh instruction receives a new session.

features.title: Governed browser tools
features.detail: Managed browser open, navigation, bounded DOM/AX snapshot and interaction paths are represented in current source and acceptance evidence.

features.title: Browser process/profile isolation
features.detail: General browser tools use a distinct Access-owned Managed Chrome process/profile from the persistent provider relay.

features.title: Native PTY terminal
features.detail: The terminal manager has completed a real node-pty PowerShell create/write/exit round-trip.

features.title: Durable recovery and reconciliation
features.detail: Ambiguous interrupted work fails closed and explicit reconciliation/quarantine preserves durable recovery evidence.

features.title: Screenshot evidence capture/storage
features.detail: Opt-in browser screenshots are hashed and stored as local diagnostics evidence; visual-model reasoning remains a separate capability boundary.

features.title: IDE/workbench shell
features.detail: The retained product UI includes local IDE, agent, provider/runtime, managed-browser, editor, terminal and MCP surfaces.
